$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Expected HID traffic for the MSI Mystic Light plugin, produced by OpenRGB's own code, not by plugin.js: Controllers/MSIMotherboardController/MSIMotherboard{185,162,112}Controller/*.cpp and RGBController_MSIMotherboard{185,162,112}.cpp at commit d4798c120659ec5ba2e664a9e87bedff8d36f880 were compiled unchanged against a scratch fake hidapi that answers GET_FEATURE 0x52 with `image` and the two firmware queries with 01 B0 <aprom> CC.. / 01 B6 <ldrom> CC.. (MinGW g++ 6.3), then driven like OpenRGB's detector and profile manager: DetectMSIMotherboardControllers() (GET 0x52, 200 bytes, pick the variant by length), the controller and RGBController constructors, ResizeZone() for each entry of `sizes`, the Direct mode selected with its own defaults (per-LED colours, brightness 10, no speed; unless `keepDeviceConfig`, which keeps what GetDeviceConfig() copied from the board) and DeviceUpdateMode(), then `frames` x DeviceUpdateLEDs() (and, with `resize`, ResizeZone() again and `framesAfter` more frames). Every LED's colour is a pattern of the frame f, the MSI_ZONE value z of its zone (JRGB1 1, JRGB2 2, PIPE1 3, PIPE2 4, JRAINBOW1 8, JRAINBOW2 9, JRAINBOW3 10, JCORSAIR 11, onboard 13) and its index i in the zone: R = (16 z + f) & 255, G = i & 255, B = (5 i + 9 z + 50 f + 1) & 255. `events` lists each hidapi call in order (hex upper case, report id first): get_feature (id, requested length, returned length), write and send_feature (bytes), read (the answer), pause (std::this_thread::sleep_for), and `mark` lines between the steps above. `openrgbZones` and `openrgbModes` are the RGBController's zones and modes right after construction. `status` is ok, firmware-invalid (no controller), no-mode (the board has no Direct mode) or unsupported-length.

scenarios.note: MPG Z490 GAMING EDGE WIFI: zones_set0, 6 onboard LEDs, 2 JRGB; strips 20 + 40 LEDs (synchronised per-LED mode); two frames
Same board with a 60-LED JRAINBOW1 strip: more than 40, so one 0x53 report per header
Same board: strips 10 + 0, then JRAINBOW1 grows to 100 while Direct is active (OpenRGB re-sends the switch once per resizable zone)
Same board, read while another program had it in per-LED mode (0x25 on the onboard master): OpenRGB's GetMode() then marks Direct active at construction
MEG Z790 ACE: zones_set16 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1-3, PIPE1, PIPE2), 0 onboard, 18 + 4 pipe LEDs, 1 JRGB; JRAINBOW3 100 LEDs
MEG Z790 ACE with a 130-LED JRAINBOW3 strip (more than 120): one report per header
TRX40-A PRO: zones_set1 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1, JRAINBOW2, JCORSAIR), no onboard zone; JCORSAIR 130 LEDs (only 120 fit the synchronised stream); corsair byte +10 read as 0x78
TRX40-A PRO whose configuration reads 240 (0xF0) at the JCORSAIR record +10: OpenRGB takes it as the JRAINBOW3 size and leaves synchronised mode
MAG B365M MORTAR: zones_set5 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1); the board's JRAINBOW2 record reads 100 LEDs, which OpenRGB counts although the board has no such zone
PRO H610M-G DDR4: zones_set11 lists JRGB1 but the board row has 0 JRGB slots, so JRGB1 and JRAINBOW1 LED 1 share stream slot 2
PRO H610M-G DDR4 with an empty JRAINBOW1: JRGB1 keeps the shared slot
MPG Z590 GODLIKE: zones_set8 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1, JRAINBOW2, JCORSAIR, PIPE1, PIPE2), 0 onboard, 15 + 18 pipe LEDs, 1 JRGB; strips 5 + 7, JCORSAIR 30; two frames
MEG X670E ACE: zones_set15 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1-3, PIPE1, PIPE2, ONBOARD), 9 onboard, 2 + 4 pipe LEDs, 1 JRGB; JRAINBOW3 45 LEDs
MPG Z390 GAMING EDGE AC: 162-byte, 10 onboard LEDs (the 10th writes the on_board_led_10 record), zones_set0
MEG Z490I UNIFY: zones_set14 (JRAINBOW1, JRAINBOW2 only); 40 + 40 LEDs is still synchronised
MPG B550 GAMING PLUS needs APROM version 6; version 5 is refused
MPG B550 GAMING PLUS with APROM version 6: zones_set2 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1, JRAINBOW2, ONBOARD), 6 onboard, 1 JRGB
MPG X570 GAMING PLUS: zone-based direct mode (one 0x52 report per frame), zones_set0, 6 onboard; JRAINBOW1 sized 1 (effects-only zone), JRAINBOW2 sized 1; two frames
PRO A620M-B: zone-based, every zone, product id >= 0x7D03 so JRGB2 uses the on_board_led_6 record and onboard LED 6 the JCORSAIR outer record; JCORSAIR colour 2 lands in the quantity/padding bytes
MEG X570 GODLIKE: zone-based, zones_set8 (JRGB1, JRAINBOW1, JRAINBOW2, JCORSAIR, PIPE1, PIPE2), no onboard LEDs
CREATOR TRX40: DIRECT_MODE_DISABLED, OpenRGB offers no Direct mode
A 185-byte board without a table row (7B16) gets OpenRGB's default: no direct mode
MPG Z790-S WIFI: per-LED, but its only zone is JRGB1, so OpenRGB sends the switch and never a colour
B450 GAMING PRO CARBON: 162-byte, 7 onboard LEDs, zones_set0 (JRGB1, JRGB2, JRAINBOW1, JCORSAIR, Onboard LEDs); two frames

B450 GAMING PRO CARBON whose first zone (JRGB1) reads as Static, brightness 5, custom colour on: with the Direct mode at its own defaults (as every scenario) the brightness is 10 and the custom-colour bit set

Same image, but the Direct mode keeps what OpenRGB's GetDeviceConfig() copied from the static first zone (brightness 5, color_mode RANDOM because of its inverted rainbow flag, so +8 bit 7 is cleared). HueDeck deliberately does not reproduce this (docs/hardware/msi-mystic-light.md); the test checks that the plugin differs from it only in those two fields
MPG Z390M GAMING EDGE AC: 162-byte, 6 onboard LEDs, zones_set2 (JRAINBOW2 is the on_board_led_10 record)
MPG B460 TRIDENT AS: 162-byte, 3 onboard LEDs, zones_set3 (JRAINBOW1, Onboard LEDs)
A 162-byte board without a table row (7D04): 10 onboard LEDs, zones_set0
112-byte board (any product id): JRGB1, JRAINBOW1, JCORSAIR, 7 onboard LEDs; zone-based direct mode; two frames
